subject.title: Discord routing: mention > reply-target > default owner (suppress default owner when targeted)

question: Should Discord multi-bot inbound routing adopt strict active-target precedence that suppresses the per-channel default owner whenever an explicit bot mention or native reply target identifies another configured bot?
rationale: The source-level gap is concrete, but the fix changes existing default-owner and binding behavior for stable multi-bot Discord deployments, so automation should not decide the product contract.

options.title: Adopt targeted precedence
options.body: Implement mention > reply-target > default-owner selection in Discord routing and add suppression tests for targeted cases.

options.title: Keep current default-owner contract
options.body: Leave default and binding routing as the primary contract and document that explicit bindings or current mention policies are required for multi-bot setups.

options.title: Narrow to reply policy only
options.body: Treat https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/80235 as the intended near-term change and leave cross-bot mention/default-owner suppression for a separate design.

recommendation.title: Adopt targeted precedence
recommendation.body: Implement mention > reply-target > default-owner selection in Discord routing and add suppression tests for targeted cases.

likelyOwner.reason: The relevant history and prior review context point to steipete across Discord preflight, shared mention policy, and routing contract decisions.
